title: Introduce configurable RAG scheduler playbook and lightweight worker samples
author: Ava Martinez
release_notes: Adds a configurable scheduler playbook for RAG deployments plus lightweight TypeScript and Go worker samples. Enables policy-driven routing for retrieval, batching and edge worker assignment.
description:
Context and motivation:
This PR introduces a small, focused playbook and example runtime for teams that want policy-driven scheduling for retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) across heterogeneous serving backends (hosted, dedicated, and edge workers). Many customers have similar patterns: retrieval latency varies by index shard and region, and downstream token cost / latency targets vary by route. Rather than bake one scheduler into the runtime, this playbook provides a reference scheduler and tiny worker shims that demonstrate: policy configuration, per-request routing heuristics, KV-cache-aware batching, and graceful fallback to local or compact models when backlog is high.

What's included (high level):
- docs/playbooks/rag-scheduler.md: playbook describing scheduler concepts, JSON/YAML policy examples, and rollout guidance.
- examples/rag-scheduler/ts-quickstart/: a TypeScript quickstart that wires a simple policy to the Redwood API and a stubbed retriever.
- examples/rag-scheduler/worker/go-worker/: a minimal Go worker that accepts scheduled tasks, demonstrates batched KV-cache reuse, and emits compact traces (zipkin-compatible).
- ci/workflows/rag-scheduler.yml: lightweight CI smoke that installs deps and runs the quickstart script.
- telemetry/presets/rag-scheduler-presets.json: suggested metric names and dashboards for the Console.
- tests/integration/rag-scheduler-smoke.test.ts: local smoke test that starts the quickstart and ensures a request path goes through scheduler -> retriever -> worker.

Small illustrative snippet (policy loader):
const policy = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(process.env.POLICY_PATH || './policy.example.json', 'utf8'))
// policy: { priorities: ["region","latency"], fallbacks: { "highLoad": "compact-model" } }

Review conversation (highlights):
- Ravi Patel (reviewer): "Nice focused playbook. Two quick asks: add a default TTL to the local KV cache sample and make the policy example explicit about 'maxConcurrentPerWorker' so teams aren't surprised by default behavior."
- Ava (author): "Added TTL and explict maxConcurrentPerWorker in policy.example.json; added comments in the TS quickstart about tuning for Dedicated vs Hosted."
- Lina Chen (reviewer): "CI failed on first run due to an integration test flakiness; can we make the test resilient to port contention? Also add a short section in the playbook about telemetry keys so Console dashboards can be imported."
- Ava (author): "Updated test to use a random local port and added telemetry preset file. Re-ran CI; all green."
- Marcus Cole (approver): "Approving — I like the clear rollout guidance and the smoke test. The Go worker is intentionally minimal which is good for teams to extend."

CI and validation notes:
- First run: Node linted and tests; integration smoke failed intermittently due to fixed port assumption (flaky).
- Fix applied: test updated to acquire a free port before starting quickstart; CI re-run passed (checks: lint, build, test, smoke).
- Telemetry preset validated locally in Console dev environment.

Backward compatibility and stability:
- No breaking changes to Redwood APIs. This PR is examples + docs + a lightweight worker shim. Marked breaking_change=false.

How to try locally (short):
1) cd examples/rag-scheduler/ts-quickstart && npm install
2) export REDWOOD_API_KEY=... && export POLICY_PATH=./policy.example.json
3) npm run start:quickstart  # starts a tiny scheduler proxy that routes to the Go worker
4) npm run smoke  # runs the local smoke test that exercises the full flow

Merge outcome:
- Merged by: Marcus Cole (squash and merge)
- Merge method: squash

Notes for maintainers and next steps:
- This playbook is intentionally small; follow-ups could include: a Python worker sample, a more complete policy editor in the Console, and an end-to-end demo that includes Dedicated capacity fallbacks.
- Suggested tracking linear tickets: ENG-2451 (scheduler enhancements), PM-612 (console policy editor).

Related: ENG-2103 (prior work on KV cache hints), SUP-1023 (customer request for region-aware routing).
